title: Ergodicity
hook: An average return can look great while your actual bank balance shrinks.
statement: What happens on average isn't what happens to you over time. Avoid any bet that could wipe you out.
explainer: A double-or-nothing bet can look good on paper. Keep taking it and you eventually hit zero. That's why survival comes before optimizing, and why spreading bets beats one big swing.
sop: List any bet where the worst case would end the business.
Drop it, even if the math looks good.
Judge growth by the compounded result, not the simple average.
Size bets so one loss can't knock you out.
Spread your risk across several bets.
equation_example: Returns of +50%, +50%, then -70%. The simple average says +10% a year. Compounded, it's (1.5 × 1.5 × 0.30) to the 1/3 power, minus 1, which is -12.3% a year. A big gap between those means one bad year is quietly sinking you.
question: Write down any bet you're making right now where the worst case would ruin you.
closing_statement: Survive first. Then let compounding do its thing.
